Subject: Partner pilot onboarding — PO requirement for Entrust Labs

Hi Jonas / Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team at Entrust is excited to pilot Redwood’s hosted inference for a 6-week integration test. Procurement is asking whether Redwood can waive the PO requirement for the pilot period and accept invoice-only for the first 60 days. Our internal PO process is taking longer than expected and we need to start provisioning next week.

Quick background: pilot budget ~USD 18,000 (estimated tokens + infra), one contractor integration, SOW attached. We can provide W-9, SOC2 Type II attestations, and a short supplier profile if that helps.

Attached: vendor_intake_form.pdf (filled).

Can you outline what paperwork we need and whether a temporary invoice-only path is possible (who signs off, what conditions)? If not possible, what’s the fastest PO route?

Appreciate it — Claire

Hi Claire — thanks for the intake form and the SOW.

Marissa is our procurement lead and Priya handles vendor intake operations; looping them in to confirm policy and next steps. High level from our side: we try to avoid invoice-only setups for production vendors, but small pilots can sometimes be approved temporarily with a short list of controls. Marissa / Priya — can you confirm the threshold and what evidence we need? Specific asks from Entrust: start provisioning next Tue (2026-11-09).

Claire — to speed this up, would Entrust be able to: 1) sign our short Pilot MSA (DocuSign), 2) share SOC2 Type II cover letter and W-9, and 3) nominate a single payment contact? If so I’ll request a temporary invoice-only exception and include a 45-day approval window.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Partner pilot onboarding — PO requirement for Entrust Labs

Thanks for the context, Jonas — Claire, welcome. I reviewed the intake form and SOW. Below is the pragmatic path we can offer for pilot customers to get started quickly while keeping procurement safeguards intact.

Summary (Redwood procurement stance):
- Default: PO required for all vendor spend once provisioning leads to billed usage.
- Exception: Temporary invoice-only (no-PO) allowed for pilot engagements if ALL of the following are provided and approved by procurement:
  * Signed Pilot MSA (DocuSign)
  * W-9 (for US entities) or equivalent tax form (for non-US)
  * Recent SOC2 Type II report (redacted acceptable) or equivalent security attestation
  * Vendor risk level <= Medium (we evaluate business continuity, data handling in intake)
  * Invoice owner contact and net-30 payment term acceptance
  * Maximum pilot cap: USD 25,000 cumulative billed during the invoice-only window

If the above are satisfied we will provision a temporary invoice-only corridor for up to 60 days. Procurement will create a short internal exception ticket that must be signed off by the Procurement Manager. If spend approaches the cap or the pilot converts to a production contract, a PO will be required before further provisioning.

Required next items from Entrust (checklist):
- Signed Pilot MSA: https://docusign.com/embedded/sign/ZXkLk2f8 (please complete by EOD Thu 11/05)
- W-9: upload to our secure intake (link in Vendor Packet)
- SOC2 cover letter or redacted report
- Primary invoice recipient name + email

Attachments: redwood_vendor_packet.pdf (includes intake upload link, required fields, and the Pilot MSA).

Operational notes:
- HubSpot deal: HS-9982345 (I attached this to the procurement ticket so we can track approvals).
- If you need faster approval (same-day), provide a PO ID from Entrust procurement and we’ll skip the exception flow.

I’ll open the exception ticket once the MSA and W-9 are in our intake system. Priya — please add risk review and route to Procurement Manager for sign-off.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Manager, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
--

Marissa / Jonas — perfect, thanks for the clear checklist and the cap. We completed the DocuSign Pilot MSA this morning and uploaded the redacted SOC2 and W-9 to the intake link in the Vendor Packet. I also attached the final SOW to this thread (entrust_sow_v1.pdf).

Quick questions:
1) Can procurement confirm the expected sign-off timeframe once the ticket is opened? We may need provisioning by 11/09 to meet the integration window.
2) If the temporary corridor is approved, will billing be consolidated to a single invoice per month, or do you send usage-based line items per product? (Our AP team prefers monthly consolidated invoices.)

We’re happy to provide a payment PO if that will dramatically speed approval — just let us know the contact at Entrust we should ask to authorize one-off PO issuance.

Thanks again — Claire
